purpose: Re-run P5C physical validation after fixing only the test-owned macOS application launch boundary: the temporary fixture is now launched as a real .app through LaunchServices and reports readiness through a temporary file. The P5C product runtime remains unchanged.
requiredClaims: The test-owned macOS fixture is packaged as a temporary .app bundle and launched through macOS LaunchServices rather than by directly spawning its inner executable.
The fixture is registered through a temporary Computer Control application Provider registry before the first Computer Control call.
No Computer Control product file or installed provider registry is modified by the test.
OPEN attempts the existing semantic operation before visual perception.
A real test-owned accessibility button is opened semantically through the existing Computer Control semantic path and independently verified without invoking P5A or the visual provider.
The visual-only test-owned target is absent from the semantic representation and produces structured NO_SEMANTIC_TARGET before any visual fallback.
Only a P5B-eligible structured semantic gap can reach the P5C visual handoff.

Visual fallback requires an execution-context object separate from planner intent with explicit allowVisualFallback=true, an injected provider, an exact visual target matching the OPEN target, a primary-display left-click request, an exact deterministic postcondition and a post-action observer.
The planner/LLM schema remains semantic and contains no visualFallback, targetQuery, provider selection or screen-coordinate fields.
A real P5A-coordinated Computer Control click returns CLICK_POSTED with semanticConsequenceVerified=false.
OPEN returns task success on the visual path only when the fresh independent post-action visual observation satisfies the deterministic exact-text postcondition and P4 returns VERIFIED_SUCCESS.
Posted delivery without verified postcondition remains NOT_VERIFIED_SUCCESS in contract coverage.
Semantic delivery failure, semantic verification failure, readiness/backend/internal/invalid failures do not become visual retries.
The physical test uses the local macOS Vision PoC only as an injected provider; P5C does not select or package a perception provider for product runtime.
Computer Use and Computer Control product trees remain clean and no screenshot bytes, OCR text or coordinates are persisted/logged by the test evidence.
nonClaims: P5C does not wire visual configuration or provider selection into the normal agent loop; that remains P5E after P5D.
P5C does not define concrete perception-provider discovery/selection; that is P5D.
The temporary application Provider exists only to let Computer Control address the test fixture semantically; it is not a P5D perception provider.
P5C does not add coordinates, native identifiers, visual queries or postconditions to planner output.
P5C does not make arbitrary OPEN failures visually eligible.
P5C does not claim general OCR accuracy, fuzzy target matching, VLM/object/icon targeting, secondary/rotated display support or richer pointer actions.
The P1-P4 physical sessions are not rerun or rewritten; their contract regressions may execute but their immutable physical evidence remains authoritative.
P5A and P5B evidence is not rewritten by this session.
P5C s01 evidence commit 15976727c6b6a09b09b428c415c5daf74e6c0258 remains immutable as the historical unregistered-fixture failure.
P5C s02 evidence commit 86793f0077d0926554c71422e4394b3bf3c62b9a remains immutable as the historical direct-executable AX snapshot failure.

evidencePolicy.onFailure: Preserve s03 unchanged, fix forward, and create s04.
evidencePolicy.sensitiveData: Fixture text and coordinates are test-owned and remain ephemeral; session output records only boolean/state claims, not screenshot bytes, OCR payloads or target/action coordinates.

onPass.nextCheckpoint: P5D concrete perception-provider delivery and selection boundary
